text:
incident-bot: PAGER: GPU nodepool capacity critical — queue length > 10k for inference-service-prod, error rate up. Priority: P0. Paging on-call for eng-oncall. runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/gpu-capacity

alex: oncall here, saw the pager. investigating. which region?

maria: region: us-east-1. metrics show token queue growth starting ~22:10 UTC, CPU fine, GPU pool saturated. several pods Pending with reason: FailedScheduling.

sam: adding logs from cluster-autoscaler, fyi:
```
I1022 22:12:01 autoscaler.go:112] ScaleUp: Launching 2 nodes in nodegroup gpu-pool-prod (min: 0, max: 50)
E1022 22:12:04 aws_manager.go:232] CreateFleet failed: UnauthorizedOperation: iam:PassRole is not authorized
caused by: failed to assume instance profile for launch template 12345
```

alex: ok that looks like IAM passrole/no permissions to create instances with the LT. did we just roll a launch template?

jordan: we pushed a launch template revision at 21:50 to switch AMI for kernel fixes. It requires attaching a new instance profile with AmazonSSM managed role. I thought the role was in place.

maria: kubectl describe pod inference-model-7f8cc Pending shows:
```
Events:
  Type     Reason             Age   From               Message
  ----     ------             ----  ----               -------
  Warning  FailedScheduling   2m    default-scheduler  0/50 nodes are available: 50 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu.
```

liam: customer-facing: we have several customers reporting high latency and 503s for streaming generation. Support queue spiking. raising bridge if needed.

alex: immediate mitigation plan: 1) try manual scale via ASG/API with an older launch template that has working instance profile 2) if IAM fails, create temporary fallback nodegroup without the new attachRole requirement 3) throttle low-priority jobs and evict non-critical pods. I'll start step 1.

sam: FYI autoscaler tried to create nodes but AWS returned: 
```
Error Code: UnauthorizedOperation
Message: You are not authorized to perform: iam:PassRole on resource: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ro-redwood-gpu-instanceprofile
```

jordan: that explains it — the new LT references role ro-redwood-gpu-instanceprofile which was created but not granted passrole to the ASG role after the last infra change. I'll check IAM immediately.

opsbot: Note: created incident channel #incident-8743210123-gpu for this thread.

alex: stepping to manual ASG create with older LT rev 17 (which uses old profile). Running:`aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name asg-gpu-prod --desired-capacity 10`

maria: check node creation events: doing `kubectl get nodes --watch`

sam: autoscaler logs show repeated attempts then backoff, so manual is necessary. If ASG create fails due to attachrole we will need to escalate to infra-iam.

jordan: confirmed — ASG attempted instances and failed with same PassRole error. That means the ASG role doesn't have iam:PassRole to the new instance profile. I can grant it but need infra approval since it's a permission change. Pinged infra-iam on pager.

liam: can we quickly spin up one-off GPU on Dedicated to drain traffic? Some customers are on Dedicated but we could re-route critical tenants to dedicated capacity if available.

alex: good idea. sam can you shift the highest-priority customer routing to dedicated pools? list of top 3 tenants: mobile-widget, embeddings-pro, search-beta.

sam: starting reroute for mobile-widget + embeddings-pro now — updating routing policy. Monitor for errors.

maria: while that happens I'm evicting batch jobs: `kubectl delete pod -l job=low-prio-batch -n inference` to free scheduling pressure.

opsbot: infra-iam acknowledged the pager — ETA 12m.

jordan: infra-iam says they can add iam:PassRole to ASG role but need a ticket/approval. I've requested emergency approval citing P0 impact.

alex: timeline: 22:20 start mitigations (manual ASG attempt + evictions + reroute). If infra can't patch in 15m we need fallback: create new nodegroup using old launch template and attach to cluster (requires kubeconfig but doable).

sam: reroute applied — mobile-widget latency back to normal on metrics for that tenant. Queue dropped ~18% for critical traffic.

maria: monitoring: pending pods still ~120, GPU utilization at 99% across pool. backpressure on request queue but critical tenants are now below SLA threshold. Good short-term.

infra-iam (via jordan): we've applied iam:PassRole to asg-role, please retry.

alex: re-triggering autoscaler/ASG create. `aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name asg-gpu-prod --desired-capacity 12`

sam: nodes are provisioning — kube shows new nodes Registering and then Ready.

maria: scheduling resumes, Pending pods decreasing. Watching for taint/label mismatch. The new nodes came up with taint `node.kubernetes.io/unschedulable=false` and label gpu=true. Good.

liam: support: customers reporting partial recovery, some still experiencing elevated latency but no widespread errors. ticket count down from 65 -> 23 since reroute.

opsbot: incident timeline updated: mitigation step 1 completed (manual ASG + IAM patch).

alex: postmortem notes to capture: cause = launch template rev referenced new instance profile that lacked proper iam:PassRole binding for ASG; autoscaler attempts failed with UnauthorizedOperation causing queue backlog; mitigation = emergency ASG desired-capacity, infra-iam permission grant, reroute critical tenants to dedicated pools, evict low-prio jobs.

jordan: we'll schedule a patch: update infra PR to ensure any new LT creation includes a validation step for PassRole and ensure CI verifies ASG role bindings.

maria: follow-ups: 1) audit recent LT changes across environments 2) add runbook step to check PassRole in preflight 3) add alert rule for autoscaler UnauthorizedOperation errors

sam: short term: keep max node limit bumped by +10 for 2 hours to soak traffic, then revert if stable. I'll coordinate with infra for rollback window.

liam: support message drafted to customers: "We're experiencing a GPU provisioning issue causing higher latencies. We've applied mitigations and are monitoring. Some customers may see intermittent elevated latencies; we'll post an update in 30 minutes." Approving, will send now.

alex: handing incident to maria for 1hr monitoring/recovery watch. I'm off-call in 20m but available on slack if needed. @maria you own bridge checkins and postmortem.

maria: ack, taking over. I'll keep this thread updated and open a postmortem doc.

opsbot: Incident severity reduced to P1 at 22:45 UTC as customer impact limited to elevated latencies for non-critical tenants.

maria: last-check: request queue down 78% from peak, GPU pool stable at 70-85% utilization. leaving the increased capacity for next 90m and then we'll scale down. Preparing postmortem skeleton.

alex: thanks all — good coordination. Closing on-call handoff.

maria: postmortem actions (short list): add LT validation, preflight PassRole test, alert on autoscaler UnauthorizedOperation, update runbook. Will assign owners in doc.

incident-bot: This thread will be archived to #postmortems after 24h unless flagged."
